cost_savings.note: Eager spawns 1 LoRA per eligible proposal (7). SPRT spawns only on BIRTH decisions (4). Of those 4 BIRTHs, oracle confirms 1 useful (TP=1) and rejects 3 as harmful/neutral (FP=3). SPRT also missed 2 oracle-positive cases (FN=2, props 5 and 6), which eager would have trained. Net: SPRT saves 3/7=42.9% of LoRAs vs eager but at the cost of missing 2/3 oracle-positive opportunities. Under proxy GT the picture flips: SPRT looks excellent because the proxy treats every APPROVED-status as positive.

summary.headline: Tab-2 SPRT: proxy GT P=1.00 R=0.80 F1=0.89; oracle GT P=0.25 R=0.33 F1=0.29. Savings vs eager: 43% of LoRA trainings avoided, but oracle says only 14% of all eligible LoRAs (1/7) are actually useful — SPRT spawns 4× too many under oracle.
